thread:
maya: Heads-up: on the prod-qa long-stream run we saw persistent memory growth in the KV cache over ~6h. Not a single leak trace, looks like micro-fragmentation + paging churn.

liam: Can you paste the profiler snapshot? rough numbers are enough.

maya: Sure — grabbed the allocator dump right after the run.
```
KV Cache Allocator Snapshot
  reserved_total: 4.19 GB
  resident_kv: 3.57 GB
  active_blocks: 129032
  free_blocks: 28912
  free_frag_pct: 21.8%
  avg_block_size: 28.6 KB
  largest_free_hole: 1.1 MB
  pages_swapped_out: 124
  compaction_runs: 3 (last at t-45m)
```

sasha: 21.8% fragmentation at that scale is painful. Are evictions triggering?

maya: Eviction threshold hit many times, but freed blocks aren't reused effectively. We keep allocating ~32KB chunks; allocator splits/merges but high churn leaves lots of small holes. Paging also kicks in for cold prefixes (pages_swapped_out).

ashwin: (typo: ashwin) Was there any recent change to slab/block size defaults or to batching heuristics? That could change allocation patterns.

maya: Yes — last week we switched kernel-selection policy to prioritize throughput on A100s which increased typical seq_len and per-request allocation lifetimes. Also batching heuristics now favor larger micro-batches for throughput. Suspect this changed lifetime distribution so reuse locality dropped.

rob: Compaction could help but heavy compaction stops are risky for tail latency. Consider incremental compaction or cooperative compaction that runs during token gaps.

liam: Agreed. Two quick ideas: 1) bump block granularity from 32KB -> 64KB and observe effect on free_frag_pct, 2) add a reuse-aging metric so reclaimed blocks aged < X are preferred for reuse before splitting.

maya: I prototyped a quick config change on dev: increased block_size to 64KB. Result: free_frag_pct dropped to ~12% but resident set grew by ~300MB and latency P95 increased ~7ms under peak. So tradeoff.

ashwin: Could we instead add a tiny background compactor that picks contiguous free ranges and coalesces into larger blocks asynchronously? That might avoid stop-the-world but still reduce fragmentation. We can cap work per second to keep tail stable.

rob: That's the incremental approach I meant. Also consider compaction triggers based on hole distribution not just percent: e.g., many small holes vs few big holes -> different strategies.

liam: We should also add a microbenchmark to reproduce the pattern: long-streams with mixed short repeated prefixes to exercise prefix reuse + long tail tokens. I can add to perf-suite. Example command: 
```
./tools/kv_stress --model test-13b --streams 150 --seq-length 40000 --prefix-rotation 5 --alloc-size 32768
```

maya: I added initial logs from that run to the thread — shows same fragmentation curve.

sasha: One more angle: eviction policy. If we bias evictions to prefer cold-but-contiguous regions rather than scattered small blocks we might lower fragmentation. Need to simulate.

ashwin: Perf regression note: the kernel-selection throughput change was rolled 3 days ago. Can we A/B rollback to confirm correlation? deploy-bot: can create a canary rollback if you want.

deploy-bot: Rollout action: canary rollback job queued for env=prod-qa, id=rb-202-1768460000.

maya: Let's do both: liam adds stress test, ashwin prototypes background compact + reuse-age policy, I will run block-size sweep and measure tail impact. We should attach results to the perf board.

rob: Add one more metric: fragmentation-induced page faults per minute. That correlates with observed pages_swapped_out spikes.

liam: I'll instrument that in the stress runner.

sasha: Sounds good. If background compactor + reuse policy fixes fragmentation we can avoid block-size growth and keep latency.

maya: OK assigning: maya -> block-size sweep + production replay; liam -> stress test + instrumentation; ashwin -> background compactor prototype (bounded work); rob -> latency safety tests. Will reconvene after first sweep. :thumbsup:
